company.shortDescription: Go Rise is a fintech platform focused on empowering migrant workers with accessible and inclusive financial services.
company.description:
Go Rise is a fintech platform focused on empowering migrant workers with accessible and inclusive financial services. The company aims to help migrants manage finances across both their home and host countries through a single digital platform.

The platform offers services such as digital bank accounts, insurance, investments, and “pay later” financial solutions in partnership with regulated financial institutions. GoRise is designed to give migrant workers greater control over their income, savings, and long-term financial growth rather than relying solely on traditional remittance services.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round
insights.statement: The latest disclosed Venture round round raised $2,100,000, or 99.55% of reported total funding.
insights.implication: This round accounts for most reported historical financing, making it important when assessing funding-source concentration and fundraising cadence.

insights.title: Meaningful non-dilutive funding
insights.statement: 1 disclosed grants total $9,530, representing 0.45% of reported funding.
insights.implication: The grants reduce the share of reported financing attributed to equity or notes, although their restrictions and milestone requirements need separate verification.

insights.title: Valuation increased across disclosed rounds
insights.statement: Known post-money valuation rose from $13,138,129 to $13,138,129, a 1x increase.
insights.implication: The disclosed financing history indicates a material valuation step-up between the earliest and latest rounds with known valuations.
caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.

insights.title: Sharp recent attention and growth momentum
insights.statement: Crunchbase scores growth at 68 (+0 over 90 days) and market heat at 64 (-7).
insights.implication: The company has recently become much more visible, but the scores should be treated as attention/activity indicators rather than revenue or clinical-performance metrics.
caveats: Crunchbase does not expose the complete weighting behind these proprietary scores.
